Discovered during LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 (llm worklog) via test-failure SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ.

## Problem
`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` and exercises the real `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, which imports `numpy` (line 117). The repo declares no Python dependency manifest (no `requirements.txt`), so on a bare interpreter the whole unit node suite fails with `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` — the failure was red on this host from 2026-10-15 until numpy was installed ad hoc during the item above.

## Goal
As a maintainer, I want the voice-input worker's Python dependencies declared (and/or the unit test to skip with a clear message when they are absent), so a fresh checkout's full suite is green without undocumented host setup.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The worker's Python runtime dependencies (numpy, faster-whisper) are declared in a committed manifest (e.g. `pi-client/voice-input/requirements.txt`) and referenced from the voice-input README setup table.
2. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` either documents the install step in its header or skips (with an explicit, non-silent message) when the resolved interpreter cannot import the required modules.
3. Full suite is green on an interpreter provisioned only from the committed manifest (verified via the test skill; no ad-hoc pip installs).

## Out of scope
Changing the worker's transcription behaviour or its stub-based test contract.

## Related
- SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ — the test-failure item that surfaced this.
- LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 — llm worklog item whose dev-push gate was blocked by it (code in SorraAgents).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MUFSJ0D3006AWP8** – Whisper worker protocol: persistent Python worker and TypeScript client (completed)
- **SA-0MUX9Y37W002T849** – voice-input: expose transcription accuracy options (beam size, VAD, initial prompt) and large-v3-turbo (completed)
- **SA-0MUYV2ZL4002TGN0** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py:197 — Unused `noqa` directive (unused: `BLE001`) (RUF100) (completed)

data.description:
# Problem statement

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` crashes with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'state_changed_flag'` when it is run against a repository with **zero detected test suites**. `state_changed_flag` is initialised inside `for cmd in commands:` (run_suite), so when `commands == []` the loop body never executes and the post-loop reference (`if state_changed_flag:`) reads an unbound local.

# Users

- **CI/CD pipeline** — the dev-push pre-push hook runs `run_tests.py --scope full` as the full-suite gate; a greenfield repo cannot push without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`.
- **Developers** — running `run_tests.py` by hand on a freshly initialised repo.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `run_tests.py --scope full --json` on a repo with no detected suites exits 0 with a defined no-suites verdict instead of crashing.
- AC2: A greenfield repo with only `.githooks` can pass the dev-push gate without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`.
- AC3: Unit tests cover the zero-suite path (`run_suite` per-suite and `run_all` aggregate), asserting the machine-readable no-suites signal.
- AC4: Documentation is updated — code comments, the `test` skill page (`skill/test/SKILL.md`) and the relevant `docs/dev/` reference.
- AC5: The full project test suite passes with the change.

# Impact

Newly initialised repositories (and any repo whose tooling yields no suites) get a clean, machine-readable "no test suites detected" verdict and can push through the standard gate instead of tripping over a runner crash or needing the documented bypass.

# Constraints

- Fix lives in the shared runner `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (no project-local override).
- Repos with one or more suites must be unaffected (regression-safe): the empty-command verdict is additive.

# Desired change

- Initialise `state_changed_flag` before the `for cmd in commands:` loop so the post-loop reference is always bound.
- Return an early, clean verdict for the zero-command case: `success=True`, `returncode=0`, `notice_code=NOTICE_NO_SUITES_DETECTED`, `notice="no test suites detected ..."`, `cached=False`, empty failure lists.
- Register `NOTICE_NO_SUITES_DETECTED` beside the other `NOTICE_*` constants; document it in the test skill page.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — guard + constant.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_zero_suites.py` — new unit tests.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (or nearest reference) — docs.

# Related work

- Code half of `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (games_curator worklog: "run_tests.py crashes on greenfield repo with zero test suites"); that item tracks the greenfield bootstrap that surfaced the crash.
- Supersedes an earlier uncommitted attempt (0MWIBGLIL00774EU) whose working-tree edit was overwritten by later `run_tests.py` commits — this item commits the fix so it cannot evaporate again.
data.title: Shared test runner crashes with UnboundLocalError on repo with zero test suites

data.description:
## User story

As an agent operating under the global guidance, I should be told explicitly that I am the owner and long-term maintainer of the codebase and that its design is my responsibility, so that I maintain long-term design health instead of only satisfying the immediate task.

## Background

Neither the global `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (installed as `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) nor `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` currently states anything equivalent to "you are the owner and long-term maintainer of this codebase, and its design is up to you".

The gap is not neutral — the existing tone actively reads the other way:

- `Coding Disciplines` items 2 and 3 ("Simplicity First", "Surgical Changes") are preservationist and, unqualified, discourage design work beyond the task.
- `Surgical Changes` explicitly says dead code is *mentioned, not deleted*, which defers maintenance indefinitely.
- The refactor skill describes itself as automated smell detection and work-item filing — hygiene performed by a tool, not stewardship exercised by an owner.

The consequence is that agents defer design responsibility: they report smells and file items rather than fixing what they touch, and they do not treat design coherence as their own problem.

## Proposed changes

### 1. `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` → `## Coding Disciplines`

- Amend item 3 (`Surgical Changes`) so dead code is *reported via a work item, or folded into the current one*, rather than silently deleted — i.e. it becomes a handled decision instead of an indefinite deferral.
- Add item 6, `**Codebase Ownership**`:

  > You are the owner and long-term maintainer of this codebase, and its design is up to you. Judge each change by the long-term health of the whole, not just by whether the immediate task compiles: maintain coherent abstractions, and leave the code better than you found it. Ownership is exercised *through* the workflow, not around it — a redesign still lands as a work item implemented via `/skill:implement`, still respects the repository boundaries in (4), and still ships with tests. Ownership is authority over *design*, never over *process*.

  The final two sentences are load-bearing: without them the clause reads as licence for unbounded redesign and contradicts items 2, 3 and 4 plus the worktree / finish gates. The clause grants design judgement, not process exemption.

### 2. `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` → new `### Ownership mindset` section after `## Overview`

Drafted text makes existing behaviour legible as ownership (fixing smells inside code you are already changing is part of the work, not scope creep), while restating that smells outside session scope still become work items, fixes still pass the test gate, and redesign lands through `/skill:implement`.

## Trade-offs considered

- **Risk of unbounded refactoring.** Mitigated by tying ownership to the workflow (work item + implement skill + test gate).
- **Conflict with `Simplicity First`.** Left adjacent and reconciled by wording in item 6 ("judged by the long-term health of the whole"). The stronger alternative — rewording item 2 to explicitly balance against whole-system design — was considered and deferred: item 6 carries that job without two edits to the same principle set.
- **Stronger wording option** (ownership outranks simplicity) is deliberately not taken, to avoid weakening the anti-speculation guard that keeps agent changes reviewable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` `## Coding Disciplines` contains an ownership principle that states, in substance, that the agent is the owner and long-term maintainer of the codebase and that its design is its responsibility.
- [ ] The ownership principle explicitly bounds itself: design authority, not process exemption; workflow (work item, implement skill, tests) and repository boundaries still apply.
- [ ] `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` item 3 (`Surgical Changes`) no longer defers dead code indefinitely — it names a handling path.
- [ ] `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` contains an `### Ownership mindset` section that frames refactoring as maintenance performed by an owner, and states that ownership does not bypass the workflow (out-of-scope smells still become work items; the test gate still applies).
- [ ] The two documents are consistent with each other and do not contradict existing principles in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`.
- [ ] No functional change to any skill script; changes are prose only.
- [ ] Full test suite passes (prose-only change, but the gate applies).
- [ ] After merge to `dev`, the operator is told to re-run `scripts/install_pi.sh` so `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` picks up the change (the installed copy is a symlink/export from this repository).

## Out of scope

- Re-running `scripts/install_pi.sh` as part of this item (it is an operator step after merge).
- Retro-establishing the principle in other skills (implement, plan, audit) — separate item if wanted.

## Notes

- Both target files are repository-boundary protected (`skill/`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`); this item is the explicit instruction that authorises the edit.
- Prose-only change: no new tests required, but existing skill-doc/lint tests must stay green.
data.title: Add explicit codebase-ownership principle to global agent guidance and refactor skill
